question: In November 2025, Austrian authorities uncovered a weapons cache in Vienna linked to a Hamas-associated network. An investigation followed that led to the arrest of a British national, identified by German prosecutors as Mohammed A., who allegedly transported the weapons to Austria after receiving them from a suspect previously detained in Germany.

In October 2025, German authorities arrested three individuals suspected of acquiring weapons from a Lebanese man who was himself caught last week after crossing the DanishGerman border. A fourth suspect was arrested after entering Germany from Czechia for supplying the latter with ammunition and weapons.

All arrested individuals are believed to belong to a terrorist organisation linked to Hamas with plans to carry out attacks against Jewish and Israeli facilities in the EU. In February 2025, four alleged Hamas members went on trial in Berlin for similar reasons. Considering the above, how is the Commission: 1.

coordinating counterterrorism measures, in addition to its new internal security strategy, with Member States and relevant external partners such as Israel to guarantee the security of all EU citizens?
planning to strictly monitor the inflow of refugees from Gaza to ensure that no former Hamas or other terrorist organisation operatives enter EU territory?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2026) While national security remains the competence of Member States, the Commission supports them. On 26 February 2026, the Commission presented the ProtectEU: Agenda to prevent and counter terrorism1.

As announced in the Agenda, the continued support of the EU agency for law enforcement cooperation (Europol) and EU agency for criminal justice cooperation (Eurojust) to Member States’ law enforcement and judicial authorities will be reinforced through the revisions of the agencies’ mandates.

The EU is also strengthening international cooperation, including through agreements on the exchange of personal data between Europol, Eurojust and priority third countries, as well as through capacity building in key regions.

Frontex also supports the security of the EU’s external borders On the same day, the Commission also presented a proposal for a directive to combat firearms trafficking and other firearms-related offences in the EU2 to improve the effectiveness of law enforcement against firearms-related crimes.

The Entry-Exit System3, which became fully operational on 10 April 2026, provides an important added layer of security against terrorist infiltration into the EU. From October 2025 until April 2026, it already allowed for the detection and barring from entering the EU of more than 600 persons considered a security threat.

The new Screening Regulation (EU) 2024/13564, which will become applicable together with the European Pact on Migration5 in June 2026, will further enhance security. It will facilitate the identification and systematic checks of third-country nationals who have crossed the external borders illegally or are staying illegally on Member States’ territory without having undergone entry checks.
